is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. and other Anopheles species (e.g., An. funestus, An. paludis) as malaria vectors in Benin (page 5, 6).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotype frequencies for Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) in Tables 4 and 5.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 4 and 5 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) and sample sizes for L1014F and G119S mutations across different communes and seasons.

african_field_population.evidence: The study involves field-caught mosquitoes from Ouidah-Kpomasse-Tori Bossito (OKT) and Adjohoun-Bonou-Dangbo (ABD) health districts in Benin (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical study conducting field collections and molecular analysis of mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data at the commune level (Ouidah, Kpomasse, Dangbo, Adjohoun, Bonou) (Table 3, 4, 5).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study specifies collection periods: OKT (August 2021 to August 2022) and ABD (July to November 2024) (page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new, independent field collections conducted between 2021 and 2024.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and bioassay data are provided in the main text tables (Tables 2, 3, 4, 5) and Figure 1.

assessment.summary: This study investigated malaria transmission and insecticide resistance in two health districts in southern Benin (OKT and ABD). It reports high frequencies of the kdr L1014F mutation and low frequencies of the Ace-1 G119S mutation in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations. Bioassays showed pyrethroid resistance with partial restoration of susceptibility using PBO.
